name: Warpaint
label: Rough Trade
lede: Two choir-class friends from Oregon and two sisters from Nevada started a band in Los Angeles on Valentine's Day 2004, went through five drummers in five years, and found the one who stuck on a night when everybody was on mushrooms.

eras.title: Sisters, choir friends and a drum stool nobody wanted
eras.text: Kokal and Wayman had been writing songs together since they were 11 in Eugene, Oregon. In Los Angeles they joined the Lindberg sisters, one of them a movie star, and spent four years playing around town before a note of it was released.

years.src: Wikipedia: Warpaint · Under the Radar · Wikipedia: Shannyn Sossamon
years.h: Warpaint, first called World War 4, forms on Valentine's Day
years.p: [[Emily Kokal|bd533fba-77a6-481c-8056-c71b9cf16b2f]], [[Theresa Wayman|81f3ecfc-aee1-4db0-9221-0ab1fd6182ff]], [[Jenny Lee Lindberg|3f8f6bb5-e3cd-4ccd-a7d8-45191b325f98]] and Lindberg's sister [[Shannyn Sossamon|a6eed316-0584-4749-af2e-e8eca4dd9e34]] start the band in Los Angeles. The name changes once they write a song called 'Warpaint'.
years.xp:
Kokal and Wayman met in choir class at 11 and wrote songs walking to school. Sossamon, a club DJ who had broken through as an actress in A Knight's Tale (2001), started out learning guitar. "No one was playing drums," she said, so she took them.

Lindberg told Guardian Music in 2011 that the band played the song 'Warpaint' for years before it finally appeared on The Fool.

years.h: Two months on a debut EP with Jacob Bercovici
years.p: Sessions for Exquisite Corpse start with producer Jacob Bercovici and run more than two months. 'Stars', 'Beetles' and 'Elephants' date from the band's first three years.

years.h: Exquisite Corpse, mixed by John Frusciante
years.p: The six-song EP comes out on the band's own. Kokal's then-boyfriend [[John Frusciante|f1571db1-c672-4a54-a2cf-aaa329f26f0b]] of the [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]] mixes it; [[Josh Klinghoffer|3f6e1477-03dc-4117-ac15-ec53b776e9a0]] drums on 'Billie Holiday' and plays guitar on 'Krimson'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shannyn Sossamon · Wikipedia: Warpaint · The Guardian (2015)
years.h: Sossamon leaves, and the drum stool starts revolving
years.p: Sossamon departs after recording the EP. David Orlando, Matthew Pacey, Klinghoffer and Michael Quinn take turns behind the kit over the next year.
years.xp: By 2015 Lindberg was tired of recounting the early revolving door of drummers, the Guardian reported, and Kokal didn't like going back to the days when Frusciante was in the mix.

eras.title: The drummer arrives on mushrooms
eras.text: A Sydney drummer with a Polish musical family walked into a party and fixed the band's longest-running problem. Within a year they were on Rough Trade, opening for the xx and on the BBC's list of the sounds of 2011.

years.h: Manimal Vinyl gives Exquisite Corpse a worldwide release
years.p: The LA indie reissues the self-released EP. In 2011 it gets to No. 4 on the UK physical singles chart.

q: She did mushrooms and played her first and last ever solo show.
years.h: Stella Mozgawa meets the band the night all of them take mushrooms
years.p: She had just come back from the desert, she said, after recording songs about candy, toast and the Grateful Dead. A friend asked her to play a show. It became her first and last solo gig.
years.xp:
Lindberg remembered crying in a corner for hours, then swimming and announcing she could see the light. She hugged Mozgawa and knocked her hat over a balcony. "That was the first time I had a conversation with you, ever!" Wayman told her.

Mozgawa, born in Sydney in 1986 to Polish parents who toured as a musical duo, had started drumming at 13 after watching Zac Hanson of Hanson.

years.h: SXSW makes them one of the week's buzz bands
years.p: Signed to Rough Trade soon after Mozgawa arrived, they play Austin's South by Southwest, and NME lists them among the ten biggest buzzes of the festival.

years.h: The Fool: Tom Biller produces, NME raves
years.p: Recorded in Los Angeles at Curves Studio and The Boat, it reaches No. 3 on the UK indie chart and later goes silver. 'Undertow' is the first single.
years.xp:
Their first NME cover called them "Satanic Majesties," Wayman remembered. The paper also quoted Kokal saying "I'm a fuck machine" when what she'd said on stage was "Look at the fog machine."

"Our first major article," Lindberg said. "We were Satanic Majesties and Emily was a fuck machine."

years.h: The BBC puts them on its Sound of 2011 list
years.p: They had spent the autumn opening for The xx in the US and Europe. Beat magazine also puts them on the cover of its winter launch issue.

years.h: Guardian Music films a live session
years.p: The band play for the paper's camera in the middle of a year of festivals: Coachella, Bonnaroo, Glastonbury, Reading and Leeds.

years.h: The Hollywood Bowl, with Arctic Monkeys and TV on the Radio
years.p: Warpaint join [[TV on the Radio|eb872766-98f6-453d-883f-2ae908a18315]], Arctic Monkeys, Panda Bear and Smith Westerns at the Bowl. A deluxe The Fool with the whole EP as a second disc follows.

eras.title: Joshua Tree, Flood and a call to the police
eras.text: With Mozgawa in from the start this time, the four wrote together, jamming songs into shape at soundchecks and in the desert. The record went top ten in the UK, and then the touring wore them down.

years.src: Under the Radar · The Guardian (2015) · Wikipedia: Warpaint
years.h: Writing in Joshua Tree, loud enough to bring the police
years.p: The first sessions for the second album happen in the desert. One elderly neighbour found 'Disco//Very' so nauseating that she called the police about the noise.
years.xp: Wayman told NME the band were after minimalism, building songs at soundchecks and trying acoustic guitars and percussion. Kokal said R&B and rap fed in, with "things that have drum machines and ambience."

yt: 'Love Is to Die', live on KEXP
years.h: 'Love Is to Die' arrives after soundtracking a Calvin Klein ad
years.p: A snippet ran in the ad that September. The song later turns up in the True Blood season finale.

years.cap: Warpaint at Stubb's, SXSW, Austin, March 2014
years.src: Wikipedia: Warpaint (album) · Under the Radar · Wikipedia: Warpaint
years.h: Warpaint goes top ten, produced by Flood
years.p: Mixed by Flood except two tracks done by [[Nigel Godrich|52de022d-5401-427f-8301-ff1b8be11a7a]]. It reaches No. 9 in the UK and No. 43 in the US.
years.xp:
Wayman on why Flood: "He's a master of lo-fi/hi-fi, really keeping the essence of the demo."

Lindberg's husband, the video artist Chris Cunningham (the subject of the song 'CC'), filmed a documentary about the sessions.

years.h: Wayman's comments on Beyoncé and Rihanna bring a backlash
years.p: Wayman called out the sexualisation of the two pop stars and fans piled on. She apologised on Facebook, then told the Observer she wished she hadn't.
years.xp: "There is truth behind what I said," Wayman said in 2015. Mozgawa backed her: "If you offend Beyoncé, people call you a racist, an anti-feminist, all these slanderous, hurtful things that aren't accurate."

years.cap: Jenny Lee Lindberg as Jennylee at the Getty Museum, Los Angeles
years.src: Magnet · The Guardian (2015) · Wikipedia: Jenny Lee Lindberg
years.h: Fifteen months on tour, then four side projects
years.p: A Hammersmith Apollo show is postponed for family matters. Lindberg makes a solo album as jennylee, Wayman forms BOSS, Kokal sings with Paul Bergmann and Mozgawa drums for [[Kurt Vile|e07a111e-4e8a-4651-a849-01ac60551ab2]].
years.xp:
"We were pretty spent," Lindberg told Magnet, and there was talk of "Maybe we don't want to do this." They kept going.

Lindberg's Right On! came out on Rough Trade that December, with Mozgawa on drums. In February the band had released 'No Way Out' and 'Riot'.

eras.title: Four nights at the Bowl
eras.text: The band came back faster and more danceable, then spent two years opening for some of the biggest acts going. When the pandemic hit, the four were scattered across three countries.

years.h: Heads Up, with drum machines after a foot injury
years.p: Jake Bercovici, who produced the first EP, comes back. Mozgawa turns to drum machines while an injured foot keeps her off the kit. It reaches No. 13 in the UK.
years.xp: The four brought songs written separately to House on the Hill in downtown Los Angeles and finished them together, January to May 2016.

years.cap: Warpaint on a festival stage, June 2017
years.h: Opening for Depeche Mode, including four Hollywood Bowl nights
years.p: They support [[Depeche Mode|8538e728-ca0b-4321-b7e5-cff6565dd4c0]] on the Global Spirit Tour through October 27. Wikipedia says the four straight Bowl dates were a first for any band.

years.cap: All Points East, Victoria Park, London, June 2018
years.h: Harry Styles takes them to Asia
years.p: A handful of support dates with Harry Styles in Asia. Wayman releases her first solo album, LoveLaws.

years.cap: Warpaint at the Echoplex, Los Angeles
years.src: The Guardian (2022) · Wikipedia: Stella Mozgawa · Wikipedia: Warpaint
years.h: Covid strands Mozgawa in Australia
years.p: She was in Reykjavík recording with [[Cate Le Bon|f2393e49-b791-46da-a6d7-1e9e60743405]] and flew home to Australia. Without a green card, she couldn't get back to her house in Joshua Tree. Kokal had given birth days earlier.
years.xp:
Lindberg had gone to Salt Lake City for what was meant to be a short break. "I didn't realise how badly I needed to slow down," she said. Mozgawa went on to co-produce [[Courtney Barnett|55111838-f001-494a-a1b5-9d818db85810]]'s Things Take Time, Take Time.

That December the band played an acoustic livestream from the Lodge Room in Los Angeles without her.

years.h: A [[Gang of Four|d8661c02-f423-4d72-8044-40ff05daf7a1]] cover for Andy Gill
years.p: Their 'Paralysed' is on the tribute album The Problem of Leisure. In April 'Lilys' arrives and lands in HBO's Made for Love.

eras.title: Not breaking up, thanks
eras.text: The fourth album took four years and two hemispheres to finish. The band spent part of the press campaign shooting down breakup talk, then marked twenty years with new songs.

q: It's not a Quentin Tarantino film. It's an album that a band made.
years.src: The Guardian (2022) · Wikipedia: Radiate Like This
years.h: Radiate Like This, finished from four home studios
years.p: Started with producer Sam Petts-Davies in early 2020, it comes out on Virgin, their first album in six years. It reaches No. 21 in the UK.
years.xp:
The band told the Guardian they were never on the verge of breaking up. "I don't remember having those conversations be public," Lindberg laughed. The record had been in the works since 2018, starting with the song 'Melting'.

Kokal, pregnant while writing, wanted "a little bit more warmth." 'Stevie' grew out of listening to Stevie Wonder.

years.src: Wikimedia Commons · Wikipedia: Radiate Like This
years.h: Rough Trade East, three days before release
years.p: The band appear at the London shop ahead of Radiate Like This, their first album away from Rough Trade.

years.h: Twenty years to the day, 'Common Blue'
years.p: The anniversary single goes up on the band's YouTube channel; 'Underneath' follows on March 21.
years.xp: "It just feels like we can conquer anything, or we can do anything, stronger together," Lindberg told Far Out. After summer US dates the band planned a break for family time.
